payload.headline: NVIDIA falls 4.12% to 156.14 before tomorrow's report; hold, no trade

summary.thesis: NVIDIA is a grade A business, and at 156.14 its price assumes slower cash-flow growth than its recent results show, but the stock is falling, has no support level below it, and reports earnings tomorrow.
summary.decision: Long-term: hold. Swing: no trade until after the 2026-11-17 report.
summary.act_at: Hold at 156.14; add near 151.37 only after a clean report; trim near 224.74

payload.happening: NVDA fell 4.12% to 156.14. It is in a downtrend, below its 20-day (195.64), 50-day (213.15) and 200-day (203.75) averages, and no support zone sits below the price. NVIDIA reports earnings on 2026-11-17. On 2026-11-16 the company announced the Rubin HPC GPU and the expanded Vera CPU platform, and said it swept the MLPerf benchmarks. A TechCrunch headline reported Sam Altman discussing 'Nvidia without Jensen Huang', which keeps the reported leadership questions in the news.
payload.business: Things that change the business: in the latest reported quarter, sales grew 105.85% from a year earlier, up from 73.21% two quarters before. Operating margin rose to 65.21% from 58.09%. Free cash flow (cash left after running and investing in the business) was 127.0B over the last year, up from 72.0B. Cash and liquidity are not a worry: net cash is 23.2B. Two things in the filings are at risk. First, margin is at the top of its 5-year range of 16–65%. Second, unpaid customer bills grew 127% while quarterly sales grew 106%, so some sales may have been pulled forward or customers may be paying more slowly. Things that change sentiment or governance: today's product news (Rubin HPC, Vera, quantum work) comes from company announcements, not filings, and gives no revenue figures, so it supports the long-term story without changing near-term numbers. The reported CEO questions and $946.6M of insider sales outside pre-set plans are governance and sentiment issues. They do not show up in demand or cash today. Segment data is not available, so data alone cannot tell us which product lines drive growth.

worth.text: At 156.14, the market is pricing free cash flow to start growing about 20.8% a year and then slow down. A discounted cash-flow model (today's value of future cash, at a 10.1% discount rate) gives 151.37 at 20% starting growth and 220.46 at 30%. The model's base case is 224.74, with a bear case of 193.13 and a bull case of 267.17. Valued on its own past price-to-sales levels, the stock comes out at 217.35–411.04, because the current price-to-sales of 12.4 sits at only the 9.0th percentile of its own 5-year range. It is also below the peer median of 16.6. The earnings multiple is 19.7 on trailing results and 9.9 on next year's estimates. The gap between methods comes down to one assumption: growth. Analysts expect 70% EPS growth next year, but the model caps starting growth at 30%. Margin is the other big lever. If operating margin falls to 48%, value drops to 113.77. At 32%, it drops to 76.17. My range is 151.37–224.74.
worth.key_assumption: Free cash flow starts growing 20–30% a year and operating margin stays near today's 65.21% instead of fading toward 48%.

bull: Quarterly sales growth sped up to 105.85% from 73.21% two quarters ago, and margin rose to 65.21%.
Next-year earnings estimates rose 23.7% over 90 days, which puts the stock at 9.9 times next year's EPS.
Price-to-sales of 12.4 is below the peer median of 16.6 and at the 9.0th percentile of its own 5-year range.
bear: Operating margin of 65% sits at the top of its 5-year range, and value drops to 113.77 if margin falls to 48%.
Unpaid customer bills grew 127% while quarterly sales grew 106%, a sign that sales may have been pulled forward.
The price is in a downtrend below the 50-day average of 213.15, with no support zone below 156.14 and insider sales of $946.6M outside pre-set plans.

levels.what: Today's close. It implies about 20.8% starting cash-flow growth, which the business has beaten recently. That is a reason to keep holding, but not to add the day before the report.
Value at 20% starting growth, the low end of the range. Add here only if the 2026-11-17 report shows operating margin near 65.21% and customer bills growing in line with sales.
Base-case cash-flow value. Near this price most of the valuation upside is used up, so reassess and consider trimming.

longterm.why: The automated rule says 'Buy now' and the business is grade A, but the committee says 'Hold', and the technical, macro and risk views are all negative. The value case supports owning the stock. The report tomorrow and the receivables warning argue against adding before the numbers are out.

swing.why: There is no support level below the price to place a stop under, and resistance sits just above at 163.9–169.14. Options price a 10.3% move by 2026-11-20, more than the 9.84 average daily range (ATR), so the report can gap past any stop.

decision.timing: No action before the 2026-11-17 report. Implied volatility of 81.0 against realized volatility of 53.9 (1.5x) shows the market expects a big move. After the report, compare revenue with the 108.7B estimate and EPS with the 2.47 estimate, and check margin and customer bills before acting at 151.37 or 224.74.

change_mind: Add instead of hold: the report beats the 108.7B revenue estimate, operating margin holds near 65.21%, and the price stays at or above 151.37.
Turn cautious or trim: operating margin falls back toward the prior 58.09%, or customer bills again grow much faster than sales (127% against 106% last time).
Swing entry: a daily close back above the 169.14 top of the first resistance zone after the report, which would end the run of lower highs.
payload.what_changed: Unchanged: still hold and no swing trade; the 4.12% drop to 156.14 brought the price nearer the 151.37 add level, but with no support below it and the report due on 2026-11-17, it is still too early to add.
payload.label: Research, not advice.
